extracted.intended_audience: investigative journalists, news organizations, and members of the public who nominate or enter journalism awards
extracted.subtask_description: Page describing IRE's annual awards programs, what each award recognizes, basic eligibility/entry scope, and what nominators must provide for consideration (e.g., IRE Awards, Philip Meyer Award, Golden Padlock, Don Bolles Medal, Ring of Honor).

rubrics_metrics.name: IRE Awards — overall recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: The IRE Awards is the annual contest of Investigative Reporters and Editors recognizing the best in investigative reporting by print, broadcast and online media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After judging, all entries are placed in IRE’s Resource Center story library so that IRE members may learn from others’ triumphs and troubles. The contest helps identify techniques and resources used by the entrants. (The 2025 contest is closed; deadline shown for 2026: Wednesday, January 21, 2026.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Philip Meyer Journalism Award — use of social research methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes the best journalism done using social research methods — techniques that are part of precision journalism, computer-assisted reporting and social science research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three awards are given annually — a first, second and third place — to recognize the best work using these techniques. Entries are placed in the IRE Resource Center to help members learn from each other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Golden Padlock Award — most secretive publicly funded agency/person
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes the most secretive publicly funded agency or person in the United States; governments at all levels — from local to federal — are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominations must provide the name of the agency or individual along with reasons and/or media coverage detailing the intransigence. The “honor” is handed out annually at IRE’s national conference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don Bolles Medal — extraordinary courage in reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes investigative journalists who have exhibited extraordinary courage in standing up against intimidation or efforts to suppress the truth about matters of public importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominations require the nominator's name, affiliation and contact information, as well as details about the nominee: link(s) to their work and a brief description of why this person merits the medal. (Established in 2017; created in conjunction with the Arizona Project anniversary.)

rubrics_metrics.name: IRE Ring of Honor — significant contributions to IRE and investigative journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Celebrates members who have made a significant contribution to the organization and to investigative journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominations can be made in tribute to current or retired IRE members or in memoriam to deceased members. The Ring of Honor is also used as a way for groups to thank colleagues while raising money to help others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination and entry procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific submission information required for nominations/entries varies by award but generally includes identifying information and supporting evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from the page: Golden Padlock nominations ask for the name plus reasons/media coverage detailing intransigence; Don Bolles nominations ask for nominator contact info, nominee name/affiliation/contact, links to work and a brief justification. General contact for questions: awards@ire.org. Buttons/forms on the site are used to submit nominations or view honorees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility scope by medium or institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility is defined by award: IRE Awards accept entries from print, broadcast and online media; Golden Padlock is limited to publicly funded agencies or persons; Philip Meyer focuses on work using social research methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page specifies the media formats and institutional eligibility per award and indicates entries/nominations are reviewed and winners presented at IRE events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archiving and educational value of entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-judging, entries (for at least some contests) are archived in IRE's Resource Center to serve as teaching examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The placement of entries in the Resource Center is framed as a key benefit: helping IRE members learn techniques and resources used to complete each story.
